data.title: Show HN: Eyesite – Experimental website combining computer vision and web design
data.author: akchro
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者因无法负担Apple Vision Pro的高昂价格，决定自制类似功能的眼动追踪网页项目——Eyesite。作者使用WebGazer.js库进行眼动校准，通过让用户注视屏幕不同位置来实现精准的眼动追踪，并用其替代鼠标操作。为了提升体验，作者去除了显示眼动位置的红色光标，使用户感觉更自然。当用户注视按钮时，按钮会有发光和弹出效果作为反馈。由于眼动追踪不够精准，作者增大了UI尺寸以提高可用性。该项目代码可在GitHub上查看，是一个有趣且具创意的实验性项目。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：眼动追踪技术在用户体验（UX）中的应用及优化

不同观点：
• [weeb] 提出两个优化眼动追踪用户体验的建议：
  1. 校准过程的优化：传统的静态点校准枯燥乏味，建议借鉴Tobii的游戏化校准方式，通过让用户与动态元素互动（如让点摇晃和爆裂）来提升趣味性，并建议通过反馈循环不断优化校准精度。
  2. 注视反馈的改进：认为不准确的小点显示可能带来负面体验，推荐Tobii的“幽灵覆盖层”方案，为用户提供近似反馈，帮助用户调整校准误差。

• [venk12] 对Tobii的追踪精度表示赞赏，并期待看到更多关于单摄像头实现眼动追踪的研究进展。

• [jll29] 引用了相关学术研究，提到了WebGaze软件（由Brown大学和Georgia Tech团队开发）以及其他关于眼动追踪在页面加载时间和搜索理解中的应用研究，提供了进一步的学术资源。

• [naveen_k] 分享了自己使用Mediapipe的眼动追踪实验，并表示对WebGazer不知情。他提到自己实现了9点移动实验，对其他人有相似的思路感到鼓舞。

• [cwmoore] 表达了对眼动追踪和情感预测技术普遍应用的担忧，认为只要有摄像头，这些技术就可能被滥用。

• [BugsJustFindMe] 提出了对应用程序最小屏幕尺寸要求的疑问，质疑其技术限制的原因。

• [holografix] 表示对实验性人机交互（HCI）项目的喜爱，认为这些项目启发了他对计算机和技术的重新思考。

• [mdrzn] 认为当前的眼动追踪技术尚不成熟（如界面晃动较大），但期待未来能够通过眼动完成阅读和导航等更自然的操作。

• [renierbotha] 建议开发基于眼动追踪的WebGL游戏，例如用眼睛瞄准，认为这将是非常酷且具有无障碍游戏潜力的项目。

• [estsauver] 简单表达了对该眼动追踪演示的赞赏，认为这是非常有趣的演示。

补充讨论：
- 技术实现的优化：讨论中多次提到Tobii的游戏化校准和反馈机制，表明这些方法在提升用户体验方面的潜力。
- 隐私和伦理问题：[cwmoore] 提到了对眼动追踪技术滥用的担忧，暗示了技术应用中的隐私问题。
- 应用场景的拓展：多个评论提到了眼动追踪技术在游戏、无障碍设计和人机交互中的潜在应用，表明该技术有广泛的应用前景。
- 学术与技术结合：[jll29] 提供了相关研究论文，显示了眼动追踪技术在学术研究中的重要性及其在实际应用中的潜力。

44253307.article_content:
Back to all posts
I wanted Apple Vision Pros, but I don’t have $3,500 in my back pocket. So I made Apple Vision Pros at home.
I was interested in making a project that combined computer vision with web design—a website that users could
physically
interact with. This inspired me to make
Eyesite
, because who needs a mouse when you have your eyes?
Eye tracking
Luckily, there is already a Javascript library for eye tracking called
WebGazer.js
. We can achieve decent eye tracking through calibration:
Make the user look at a point and click. This maps the current gaze to a point on the screen.
Feed the gaze/coordinate mapping into WebGazer to calibrate.
Repeat 9x times on the corners, sides, and center to get good mapping data.
I found that it was best to get 5 mappings per point for better eye tracking accuracy.
Calibration in debug mode. The top right shows how WebGazer tracks your eyes and face. The red dot is where it thinks I’m looking.
Website Interaction
Now that we have eye tracking, we can make some cool things with it! I decided to use the user’s gaze as a mouse and have them click with spacebar—kind of like how Apple Vision Pros have you look and pinch. Although I had the main functionality, it was far from finished. There were many considerations with making the experience as smooth and immersive as possible.
The “Invisible” Mouse
Initially, the user could see “where” they were looking at through a red dot.
Main page in debug mode.
This created some problems. First, the red dot was distracting, and users would unconsciously look at it instead of my buttons. Second, the red dot revealed how inaccurate the eye tracking was, which ruined the immersion.
Ultimately, I decided to remove the “eye cursor” and also make the user’s mouse invisible. It made you really feel like you were controlling the website with your eyes rather than moving a mouse around. You can turn on debug mode to see your eye cursor and mouse.
User feedback
Since we don’t have a mouse, we need some way for the user to know they are looking at something. To do this… we track the user’s gaze (how surprising). We hid the eye cursor, but we still have the x and y coordinates of the user’s gaze. Each button component has checks to see if that gaze is within its borders. When the component detects the user is looking at it, it responds with a slight glow and pop.
Large UI
Admittedly, the eye tracking is not the best. You can really see how jittery it is with debug mode on. So I decided to make the UI huge. I also added a screen size restriction so the site is only usable on displays that meet a minimum size threshold (Sorry mobile users! It wouldn’t work on your phone anyway).
The large size of the button accounts for the jitteriness of the eye tracking.
Conclusion
Those were a few details about Eyesite. If you are interested, you can see the source code. Small warning: this project was just a small demo and isn’t a shining example of clean code or best practices.
This was a really fun project to make, and super cool to use too. If you want to make your own computer vision project or improve this one, I encourage you to do so! You can find the project at
https://github.com/akchro/eyesite
.

data.title: TV Fool: See OTA channels you can receive
data.author: nvahalik
data.article_summary: 该网站提供多种工具和服务，帮助用户分析和查找电视及FM广播信号。主要功能包括电视信号定位、在线电视地图、Google Earth电视地图、呼号查询、信号分析和覆盖图常见问题解答等。此外，网站设有论坛和反馈渠道，方便用户交流和报告数据错误。用户可以通过这些工具获取详细的信号信息和地图数据，以改善电视和广播接收效果。网站还包含新闻和常见问题解答，帮助用户更好地理解和使用其服务。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：ATSC 3.0信号的接收、加密问题以及相关网站的使用体验

不同观点：
• [jakedata] 认为ATSC 3.0信号中的Widevine DRM加密使得大多数频道无法通过网络电视调谐器观看，称其为"公共资源私有化"的愚蠢行为，并表达了对FCC可能批准这一做法的不满。他还提到目前只有一个未加密的ATSC 3.0信号可以观看，且DVR功能因此被禁用。

• [1317] 提出是否有类似英国官方网站（如freeview.co.uk）的平台，能够提供接收检查和完整的电视指南，以帮助用户更好地接收OTA（无线）电视信号。

• [aidenn0] 对某个用于检查信号接收的网站提出具体技术性问题，指出该网站未准确反映地形对信号接收的影响，并且对有效辐射功率（ERP）的显示不准确，认为其使用的是授权ERP而非实际ERP。

• [m0d0nne11] 对tvfool.com网站要求安装浏览器插件表示不满，明确表示不愿意安装插件。

• [iqfareez] 关注该类服务的可用国家范围，询问在哪些国家可以使用这些服务。

• [johng] 提到该网站的数据库自2017年后未更新，对网站的实用性表示了一定失望，但仍对网站的功能表示认可。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及的具体技术问题包括ATSC 3.0的DRM加密对电视信号接收的影响、地形对信号接收的作用，以及网站数据准确性等问题。
• 不同用户对网站的使用体验和功能需求存在差异，部分用户关注技术细节，部分用户则关注网站的实用性和更新频率。
• 争议的焦点在于ATSC 3.0信号加密对公共资源使用的影响，以及用户对加密技术带来的不便表达了不满。

data.title: The curious case of shell commands, or how "this bug is required by POSIX" (2021)
data.author: wonger_
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了在Linux和UNIX系统中使用诸如`bash`、`ssh`、`i3`、`screen`、`tmux`、`dtach`等工具时，它们通常依赖`system(3)`函数通过`sh -c`执行命令，而不是直接调用`execve(2)`。这种设计可能导致安全问题，特别是在处理用户输入时，未经过滤的输入可能引发shell注入风险。文章提醒开发者在编写脚本和工具时需谨慎处理命令和参数，进行适当的转义和引用，以避免潜在的安全漏洞。尽管这个问题在多个操作系统的工具中普遍存在，但相关文档如POSIX手册中并未充分强调这一风险，因此开发者需格外注意。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于`system()`函数及其安全性问题的不同观点和讨论

不同观点：
• panzi观点：认为`system()`应该被废弃，特别是在新程序中不应使用。原因在于不同操作系统（如POSIX和Windows）对命令行解析的不一致性，尤其是在Windows中，每个程序可能有不同的解析方式。Rust对相关问题有明确警告，但Java等其他语言则没有。

• o11c观点：反对完全弃用`system()`，认为在某些情况下将命令传递给shell是必要的功能，例如`popen("gzip > foo.gz")`。任何涉及用户输入的情况都应事先进行 sanitize。批评文章中对`ssh`的指责，认为其作为shell命令执行工具并无不妥。

• GuB-42观点：`system()`有其存在的意义，适用于需要shell功能如管道的情况，类似于POSIX世界中的`eval()`。在安全性方面，若使用`system()`处理用户输入，相当于给予用户shell权限，需谨慎使用，或选择`exec*()`等替代方法。

• chubot观点：强调`printf '%q '`等工具在命令行参数引用中的重要性，并指出shell对参数的错误处理（如`ssh`的隐式`argv`连接）是安全问题的根源。提出shell设计缺陷，并建议Oils shell引入新的`invoke`内建命令来解决此问题。

• endiangroup观点：分享其在处理`ssh`命令限制工具中的经验，指出虽然其工具依赖于shell执行命令，但通过限制命令参数传递来缓解安全问题。

• pabs3观点：提到命令行选项允许代码执行的问题，并引用相关资料进行说明。

• Wicher观点：为解决`ssh`命令参数传递问题，提供了一个自制的pseudoshell工具，以便更安全地传递参数向量。

• ptx观点：认为shell命令执行问题并非Linux特有，而是UNIX体系的普遍问题。引用FreeBSD文档中的安全考虑说明。

• a_t48观点：推荐使用Python的`shlex.quote`来处理命令行参数引用问题，但强调最好的解决方案是尽可能避免使用shell命令。

• 1vuio0pswjnm7观点：讨论了不同shell（如bash和dash）的使用场景和性能差异，提出使用轻量级shell（如Almquist shell）的优点。

• 0xbadcafebee观点：认为文章讨论的问题是学习*NIX系统和shell脚本的常见困难，属于学习曲线的一部分，建议加强相关教育。

• blueflow观点：指出文章中对"command"和"argument vector"的混淆，认为这是导致误解的原因。

• zahlman观点：通过实验说明Python中调用shell命令与直接使用shell的不同表现，并提出如何处理特殊命令名称（如`-x`）的问题。

补充讨论：
• hackernudes观点：认为文章难以 follow，但同意`${var@Q}`和`printf '%q'`是有效的解决方案，希望能看到更多明显的引用方式以简化嵌套shell调用的处理。

44236241.article_content:
Some context
(For those interested only in the
glibc
and POSIX issues, see
at the end
.)
I use Linux almost everywhere, from laptops and desktops to servers and routers, and over the course of many years I've written quite a few
bash
scripts that ease my interaction with all of these.
The usual "stack" that ties all of these together is composed of:
bash
, obviously for scripting;
ssh
, for remote execution;
i3
, the window manager for desktop environments;
screen
, for terminal multiplexing;
tmux
, for terminal multiplexing;
dtach
, for launching processes in background while still being able to access them if needed;
(among many other tools like
coreutils
and friends,
grep
,
sed
,
sort
,
find
,
xargs
,
rsync
, plus other smaller C, Go or Rust based tools; but all of these are not the subject of this article;)
What do all of the former have in common? They all provide some sort of functionality, but by themselves they don't actually do anything; they are meant to delegate the actual work to other tools.
So what is the problem you ask? Nothing really... Everything is fine... No planes are falling from the sky... Nobody is running around screaming while on fire...
Everything is business as usual,
unless you want to write some wrapper scripts that takes arbitrary user input and delegates that to one of these, and many other, broken tools
...
And just for completeness I'll throw in some other tools that fit the bill:
make
(and any other variant or derivate), for build systems;
ninja
, my favorite build system, and lightweight DAG job scheduler and executer;
Root of all evil
As many of you have guessed, because we live in a UNIX world, many of these tools delegate the actual tool execution to the
glibc
system(3)
function,
which ends-up calling
sh(1p)
(most likely
bash
) with the
-c
argument.
As opposed to doing the correct thing and just calling
execve(2)
...
BTW, this is not something Linux specific. Unfortunately it is a trait inherited from the UNIX ancestry by almost all operating systems, including all BSD variants plus OSX;
and, for some tools, this behavior is even seen when running on Windows.
But I digress...
Excerpts from Linux
system(3)
man page
Let's quote from the Linux
system(3)
man page:
The
system(3)
library function uses
fork(2)
to create a child
process that executes the shell command specified in command
using
execl(3)
as follows:
execl("/bin/sh", "sh", "-c", command, (char *) NULL);
[...]
Any user input that is employed as part of command should be
carefully sanitized, to ensure that unexpected shell commands or
command options are not executed. Such risks are especially
grave when using
system()
from a privileged program.
So far the warning doesn't sound very comforting...
But hey, we are all responsible developers...
Excerpts from POSIX
system(3p)
man page
Let's quote from the POSIX
system(3p)
man page:
Hmm... Strange... There is nothing to quote from this manual about warnings, issues or sanitization...
(Except perhaps the warning for set-UID or set-GID processes against using this function, due to potential privilege escalation issues.)
Excerpts from POSIX
sh(1p)
man page
How about quoting from the POSIX
sh(1p)
man page regarding the
-c
flag:
-c
-- Read commands from the command_string operand. Set the
value of special parameter 0 (see Section 2.5.2,
Special Parameters) from the value of the command_name
operand and the positional parameters (
$1
,
$2
, and so
on) in sequence from the remaining argument operands.
No commands shall be read from the standard input.
OK... Still nothing about warnings, issues or sanitization...
Excerpts from
bash(1)
man page
Perhaps we'll have more luck quoting from the
bash(1)
man page:
-c
-- If the
-c
option is present, then commands are read from
the first non-option argument command_string. If there
are arguments after the
command_string
, the first argument
is assigned to
$0
and any remaining arguments are assigned
to the positional parameters. The assignment to
$0
sets
the name of the shell, which is used in warning and error
messages.
Hmm... Perhaps sanitization isn't that a big of an issue?
Partial conclusion
For now let's remember that initial remark:
Any user input [...] part of command should be [...] sanitized [...].
Aside from that, perhaps this "shell command" business I'm crying about isn't such a big of an issue?
Else the POSIX manuals for
system(3p)
(~2K words) and
sh(1p)
(~8K words)
-- that I assume were written by legions of committee members -- would have certainly spared at least a few words about this issue...
Right?
Unintended consequences
So why do we care about
system(3)
and
sh -c
?
Because as said in the beginning, many tools accept as arguments commands which in the end are passed to
sh -c
via the
system(3)
function.
Therefore when we write our scripts and tools we need to be aware of this situation and be prepared to escape and quote our commands and arguments accordingly,
else we'll be subject to
shell injections
... (For more sc
44236241.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了在Linux和UNIX系统中使用诸如`bash`、`ssh`、`i3`、`screen`、`tmux`、`dtach`等工具时，它们通常依赖`system(3)`函数通过`sh -c`执行命令，而不是直接调用`execve(2)`。这种设计可能导致安全问题，特别是在处理用户输入时，未经过滤的输入可能引发shell注入风险。文章提醒开发者在编写脚本和工具时需谨慎处理命令和参数，进行适当的转义和引用，以避免潜在的安全漏洞。尽管这个问题在多个操作系统的工具中普遍存在，但相关文档如POSIX手册中并未充分强调这一风险，因此开发者需格外注意。
44236241.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于`system()`函数及其安全性问题的不同观点和讨论

不同观点：
• panzi观点：认为`system()`应该被废弃，特别是在新程序中不应使用。原因在于不同操作系统（如POSIX和Windows）对命令行解析的不一致性，尤其是在Windows中，每个程序可能有不同的解析方式。Rust对相关问题有明确警告，但Java等其他语言则没有。

• o11c观点：反对完全弃用`system()`，认为在某些情况下将命令传递给shell是必要的功能，例如`popen("gzip > foo.gz")`。任何涉及用户输入的情况都应事先进行 sanitize。批评文章中对`ssh`的指责，认为其作为shell命令执行工具并无不妥。

• GuB-42观点：`system()`有其存在的意义，适用于需要shell功能如管道的情况，类似于POSIX世界中的`eval()`。在安全性方面，若使用`system()`处理用户输入，相当于给予用户shell权限，需谨慎使用，或选择`exec*()`等替代方法。

• chubot观点：强调`printf '%q '`等工具在命令行参数引用中的重要性，并指出shell对参数的错误处理（如`ssh`的隐式`argv`连接）是安全问题的根源。提出shell设计缺陷，并建议Oils shell引入新的`invoke`内建命令来解决此问题。

• endiangroup观点：分享其在处理`ssh`命令限制工具中的经验，指出虽然其工具依赖于shell执行命令，但通过限制命令参数传递来缓解安全问题。

• pabs3观点：提到命令行选项允许代码执行的问题，并引用相关资料进行说明。

• Wicher观点：为解决`ssh`命令参数传递问题，提供了一个自制的pseudoshell工具，以便更安全地传递参数向量。

• ptx观点：认为shell命令执行问题并非Linux特有，而是UNIX体系的普遍问题。引用FreeBSD文档中的安全考虑说明。

• a_t48观点：推荐使用Python的`shlex.quote`来处理命令行参数引用问题，但强调最好的解决方案是尽可能避免使用shell命令。

• 1vuio0pswjnm7观点：讨论了不同shell（如bash和dash）的使用场景和性能差异，提出使用轻量级shell（如Almquist shell）的优点。

• 0xbadcafebee观点：认为文章讨论的问题是学习*NIX系统和shell脚本的常见困难，属于学习曲线的一部分，建议加强相关教育。

• blueflow观点：指出文章中对"command"和"argument vector"的混淆，认为这是导致误解的原因。

• zahlman观点：通过实验说明Python中调用shell命令与直接使用shell的不同表现，并提出如何处理特殊命令名称（如`-x`）的问题。

补充讨论：
• hackernudes观点：认为文章难以 follow，但同意`${var@Q}`和`printf '%q'`是有效的解决方案，希望能看到更多明显的引用方式以简化嵌套shell调用的处理。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[机械设备的标准化描述及具体应用]

不同观点：
• [downboots] 提出是否存在一种标准化的方式来描述机械设备，类似于用 .obj 文件定义3D形状。他希望这种标准能够描述零件类型、交互、属性、运动范围等，并希望计算机能够利用这种格式从类似 https://507movements.com/ 的目录中找到有趣的配置，结合模拟（如迪士尼研究项目中齿轮和连杆的模拟）来实现。

• [burnt-resistor] 对望远镜式吊臂内部结构感兴趣，尤其是多节结构可以相互嵌套。他提到澳大利亚的 CEE 频道正在修复一台 Frena 起重机，通过禁用一些不必要的部分来简化操作，尽管这样做会牺牲一些负载能力和稳定性。

• [EricRiese] 提出了一个创意，希望能看到有人用这种机制制作一个"复合长号"（compound trombone）。

• [edweis] 则关注这些机械结构是否在工业层面得到应用，提出了对该技术实际工业用途的疑问。

补充讨论：
• [downboots] 关注的是机械设备描述的标准化和计算机辅助设计与模拟的可能性，强调了标准化格式对机械设计自动化的重要性。

• [burnt-resistor] 通过具体实例（望远镜式吊臂）展示了多节结构的实际应用和其在特定情况下的实用性。

• [EricRiese] 从一个创意角度出发，提出了将机械结构应用到乐器设计中的可能性。

• [edweis] 则更关注这些技术的实际工业应用，反映了讨论从理论和创意到实际应用的延展。

争议焦点：
• 目前没有明确的争议，但不同参与者关注的角度不同，有的关注理论和标准化，有的关注实际应用，还有的从创意角度出发。这反映了讨论在理论与实际应用之间的张力。

data.title: Navy backs right to repair after $13B carrier goes half-fed
data.author: beardyw
data.article_summary: 美国海军和陆军正在推动“维修权”，以解决因合同限制导致军方无法自行修理设备的问题。海军部长约翰·费伦在参议院作证时提到，价值130亿美元的USS Gerald R. Ford航母因合同限制无法修理故障的六个烤箱，导致无法为4500名船员提供充足的餐食。此外，航母的武器升降机也因类似问题延迟四年才完全运作。陆军同样面临类似困扰，国防部长指示将“维修权”条款纳入合同。参议员伊丽莎白·沃伦提出的《军人维修权法案》正在国会审议。军方强调，士兵有能力修理自己的设备，不应依赖第三方承包商。这一行动也可能推动联邦层面的“维修权”立法。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于“维修权”在军事设备（特别是海军舰艇上的烤箱）上的适用性和实际操作性讨论，涉及合同限制、责任归属、设备复杂性以及海军自我维修能力的问题。

不同观点：
• **Perihelions** 认为，评论中讨论的“维修权”与通常理解的不同。通常“维修权”意味着供应商有义务提供文档或零件，但这里的案例是，使用方签订了禁止自行维修设备的合同。因此，这不是典型的“维修权”问题，而是合同限制问题。
  
• **Atonse** 强调了这一情况的荒谬性，尤其是在战争背景下。拥有强大军事力量的舰艇上，士兵们却因为合同限制无法自行修理设备，导致基本生活保障（如食物供应）出现问题，这是非常令人担忧的。

• **DrScientist** 指出，如果设备（如烤箱或运送核武器的升降机）出现故障，无法自行修理而必须等待外部承包商来维修是极其不合理的。这引发了对谁签署了这些限制性合同的质疑。

• **Uticus** 认为，虽然海军拥有维修权可能会解决一些问题，但这也会带来新的责任和官僚程序。海军内部的繁琐程序可能会使问题变得更加复杂，最终仍然需要依赖外部承包商。

• **Vfclists** 持更为激烈的批评态度，认为这是海军和供应商腐败的体现。他们质疑为何海军不设计自己的设备，而是依赖外部供应商，并指出这种依赖可能对国家防御产生严重影响。

• **Dhx** 提供了技术细节，指出现代舰艇上的烤箱设备非常复杂，可能需要专业培训和工具来进行维修。此外，舰艇上的空间和操作限制可能使得自行维修变得不切实际。同时，他们也提到海军可能缺乏实际维修经验，这使得自行维修更加困难。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于合同限制和设备复杂性是否合理，特别是在军事背景下，这种限制是否会对国家防御产生负面影响。
• 另一个讨论点是海军是否应该设计自己的设备以避免依赖外部供应商，以及在现代设备复杂性增加的情况下，自我维修是否可行。
• 还有人担心海军内部的官僚程序可能会使得自我维修变得更加复杂，而不是解决问题。

US Navy backs right to repair after $13B carrier crew left half-fed by contractor-locked ovens
54
Army joins in push to break vendor grip on military maintenance
Iain Thomson
Wed 11 Jun 2025
//
21:56 UTC
US Navy Secretary John Phelan has told the Senate the service needs the right to repair its own gear, and will rethink how it writes contracts to keep control of intellectual property and ensure sailors can fix hardware, especially in a fight.
Speaking to the Senate Armed Services Committee on Tuesday, Phelan cited the case of the USS Gerald R. Ford, America's largest and most expensive nuclear-powered aircraft carrier, which carried a price tag of
$13 billion
. The ship was struggling to feed its crew of over 4,500 because six of its eight ovens were out of action, and sailors were barred by contract from fixing them themselves.
"I am a huge supporter of right to repair," Phelan
told
the politicians. "I went on the carrier; they had eight ovens — this is a ship that serves 15,300 meals a day. Only two were working. Six were out."
He pointed out the Navy personnel are capable of fixing their own gear but are blocked by contracts that reserve repairs for vendors, often due to IP restrictions. That drives up costs and slows down basic fixes. According to the Government Accountability Office,
about 70 percent
[PDF] of a weapon system's life-cycle cost goes to operations and support.
A similar issue plagued the USS Gerald Ford's weapons elevators, which move bombs from deep storage to the flight deck. They reportedly took more than
four years
after delivery to become fully operational, delaying the carrier's first proper deployment.
"They have to come out and diagnose the problem, and then they'll fix it," Phelan said. "It is crazy. We should be able to fix this."
The Navy is not alone in its concerns, as the US Army is
peeved
about the right to repair equipment it paid for too. In a rare display of bipartisanship, both Democrats and Republicans agreed that the Army shouldn't be waiting on contractors to fix its kit and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth issued a memo directing the service to add right-to-repair provisions to its contracts.
"On a go-forward basis, we have been directed to not sign any contracts that don't give us a right to repair," Army Secretary Daniel Driscoll told the House Armed Services Committee on June 4. "On a go-back basis, we have been directed to go and do what we can to go get that right to repair."
Last year Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-MA) introduced the
Servicemember Right-to-Repair Act
[PDF] that would allow military personnel to repair the equipment they use. It's currently under consideration by Congress, but it seems the government is anxious to move fast.
Our soldiers are immensely smart and capable and should not need to rely on a third party contractor to maintain their equipment. Oven repair is not rocket science
"Our soldiers are immensely smart and capable and should not need to rely on a third party contractor to maintain their equipment. Oven repair is not rocket science: of course sailors should be able to repair their ovens," Kyle Wiens, CEO of repair specialists iFixit told
The Register
.
"It's gratifying to see Secretary Phelan echoing our work. The Navy bought it, the Navy should be able to fix it. Ownership is universal, and the same principles apply to an iPhone or a radar. Of course, the devil is in the details: the military needs service documentation, detailed schematics, 3D models of parts so they can be manufactured in the field, and so on. We're excited that the military is joining us on this journey to reclaim ownership."
Liz Warren, Trump admin agree on something: Army should have right to repair
The state of Right to Repair: Progress made, but key barriers remain
Oh, Deere! FTC sues tractor maker, alleging decades of monopolized repairs
Canada passes new right to repair rules with the same old problem
Wiens has also been vocal in letting ordinary citizens have the same rights, despite frantic lobbying by the tech industry, which would generally prefer you just buy a new thing when the old one wears out.
Several states
, including California, New York, Massachusetts, Minnesota, Oregon, and Colorado, have already passed consumer right-to-repair laws, and now it seems like the military is leading the way to get it done on the federal level.
"We hope that anyone listening to us who hopes to pitch us a contract going forward will look back at their previous agreements they've signed with us, and if they're unwilling to give us that right to repair, I think we're going to have a hard time negotiating with them," Driscoll said.
We'll have to see if this trickles down to the rest of us. ®

• **Perihelions** 认为，评论中讨论的“维修权”与通常理解的不同。通常“维修权”意味着供应商有义务提供文档或零件，但这里的案例是，使用方签订了禁止自行维修设备的合同。因此，这不是典型的“维修权”问题，而是合同限制问题。
  
• **Atonse** 强调了这一情况的荒谬性，尤其是在战争背景下。拥有强大军事力量的舰艇上，士兵们却因为合同限制无法自行修理设备，导致基本生活保障（如食物供应）出现问题，这是非常令人担忧的。

• **DrScientist** 指出，如果设备（如烤箱或运送核武器的升降机）出现故障，无法自行修理而必须等待外部承包商来维修是极其不合理的。这引发了对谁签署了这些限制性合同的质疑。

• **Uticus** 认为，虽然海军拥有维修权可能会解决一些问题，但这也会带来新的责任和官僚程序。海军内部的繁琐程序可能会使问题变得更加复杂，最终仍然需要依赖外部承包商。

• **Vfclists** 持更为激烈的批评态度，认为这是海军和供应商腐败的体现。他们质疑为何海军不设计自己的设备，而是依赖外部供应商，并指出这种依赖可能对国家防御产生严重影响。

• **Dhx** 提供了技术细节，指出现代舰艇上的烤箱设备非常复杂，可能需要专业培训和工具来进行维修。此外，舰艇上的空间和操作限制可能使得自行维修变得不切实际。同时，他们也提到海军可能缺乏实际维修经验，这使得自行维修更加困难。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于合同限制和设备复杂性是否合理，特别是在军事背景下，这种限制是否会对国家防御产生负面影响。
• 另一个讨论点是海军是否应该设计自己的设备以避免依赖外部供应商，以及在现代设备复杂性增加的情况下，自我维修是否可行。
• 还有人担心海军内部的官僚程序可能会使得自我维修变得更加复杂，而不是解决问题。

最终，作者对TDD持保留态度，认为测试无法解决“知道该做什么”的根本问题。

Reflections on Sudoku, Or the Impossibility of Systematizing Thought
I reflect on the Entscheidungsproblem how it relates to Sudoku solvers. It's a little weird.
.
The other day, to no one's surprise, I was fumbling over a programming problem.
This wasn't anything satisfyingly algorithmic, but more the thing where you're
evaluating a million questions on "how should I structure this system?". While
I'm no design purist, I like to at least make an attempt at sketching out the
problem space and think through options before I just start coding something. My
rule of thumb for this is, let's call it the "10% rule" - make sure I try to
think hard about a problem for 10% of the time before I start playing around
with code. Writing code helps clarify many things but it's also easy to get
stuck in local minima
I have the same problem when writing text, like this blog post. Put me in front of an editor and I'll pointlessly recraft sentences instead of getting the thing finished.
. This rule helps keep me from getting lost too early,
but I often think about whether I could do better.
I'd like to say I have a systematic process I apply here. I don't. I think
over one idea, then another,
writing down my thoughts
,
but it's always hard to feel like you're making a lot of progress.
It's honestly frustrating. I often wish I could "systematize" it somehow,
applying some rigorous method and march towards the solution. Could I become one of
those
magic people
who just sit down in front of a problem and watch it decompose in front
of them?
Over time I've accepted that is impossible. There is no person, no process,
which can systematize thought. Millions of math problems
elude
Terence Tao
despite his brilliance.
Now I see these differences in aptitude as having different sets of
mental tools at your disposal. The more tools you have, the better tools you
have, and the better you are at applying them, then the better you get at
certain problems. Maybe your background makes you better or more interested in
different tools. But we can all learn new tools, and get better at the ones we
have.
This is all kind of murky and unsatisfying though. Wouldn't it be nice if you
just had a general method you could apply to solve everything? What happens if
you
think
you have a method to solve all problems?
The Sudoku Affair
A few months ago I read Zach Tellman's fascinating article on the
Sudoku
Affair
, in which he revisited Peter Norvig & Ron
Jeffries very, very different attempts to produce a workable Sudoku solver. (I
highly recommend reading the original article as well, as Zach's deep analysis
of Ron Jeffries attempts at producing a Sudoku solver is fascinating).
Some background: Ron Jeffries made a career advocating for test-driven
development (TDD) and extreme programming. Peter Norvig is a research lead at
Google and author of many papers and a few books on AI. As you'd expect, this
leads to different approaches to problems.
Ron Jeffries attempted to solve Sudoku by approaching it
"rigorously"
No offense intended, but just being clear this isn't like
mathematical rigour
but more of an applied philosophy.
from the perspective of TDD. He outlines the
problem, writes a test case and begins to iterate, adding tests and refactoring.
In the initial set of posts, he can't get to a real solution despite many hours
of effort. He then revisited the problem 20 years later, and in the end spends
50
posts
writing about the process of building a solver. At some point, he
finds code from another site
and starts to bring that into the fold. He eventually gets to a solution, though at
that point I honestly have trouble figuring out how much TDD had to do with the process.
Peter Norvig takes a different approach, analyzing the high-level problem and
then breaking down the data structures and outlining the solution in the course
of ~20 lines of code. While his code might be a bit dense to follow initially,
the way he approaches the problem and pre-builds data structures makes "testing"
trivial. His test for validity is part of the search condition for his program.
It's hard not to appreciate the systematic nature of Peter's approach: define
the problem, look through your toolkit, apply the relevant tools, success. Of
course, Peter has an advantage that he's
written
books
about related techniques.
Ron Jeffries attempt definitely didn't make me excited about TDD, I at least
respected that he didn't try to hide things after the fact.
Many people have commented about this over time, with lots to say
about TDD and programming. In Peter Siebel's post on
Unit testing in Coders at Work
even Peter Norvig chimes in, indicating he's not "anti-test", but that tests don't fix the
underlying issue of "knowing what to do."
Then bloggers were arguing back and forth about what this means. I don’t think
it means much of anything—I think test-driven design is great. I do that a lot

data.author: lentoutcry
data.article_summary: 一项由奥胡斯大学和牛津大学合作进行的研究发现，当人们听到持续的节奏或音乐时，大脑不仅被动接受声音，还会实时重组其内部网络。研究引入了一种名为FREQ-NESS的新型神经影像技术，能够通过独特频率识别和追踪大脑网络的活动。这种方法揭示了不同声音频率如何像波浪一样在大脑区域间传播，提供了对感知、注意力甚至意识的全新理解。该技术为精确脑图绘制打开了大门，可能革新基础神经科学、脑机接口和临床诊断。研究结果表明，大脑在响应声音时会进行动态重构，而不仅是简单反应。

Dancing brainwaves: How sound reshapes your brain networks in real time
What happens inside your brain when you hear a steady rhythm or musical tone? According to a new study from Aarhus University and the University of Oxford, your brain doesn't just hear it--it reorganizes itself in real time.
Date:
June 2, 2025
Source:
Aarhus University
Summary:
Listening to sound doesn t just trigger brain activity it reshapes your brain s internal networks in real time. Scientists have unveiled a powerful new imaging method, FREQ-NESS, that traces how different sound frequencies ripple through brain regions like shifting waves. This discovery could revolutionize how we understand perception, attention, and even consciousness.
Share:
Facebook
Twitter
Pinterest
LinkedIN
Email
FULL STORY
Your brain dances to music more than you think — it reconfigures itself in response to sound. A new technique reveals how rhythmic tones spark shifting brainwaves across neural networks. Credit: Shutterstock
What happens inside your brain when you hear a steady rhythm or musical tone? According to a new study from Aarhus University and the University of Oxford, your brain doesn't just hear it -- it reorganizes itself in real time.
Every beep, tone and new sound you hear travels from the ear to registering in your brain. But what actually happens in your brain when you listen to a continuous stream of sounds? A new study from Aarhus University and University of Oxford published in
Advanced Science
reveals that the brain doesn't simply register sound: it dynamically reshapes its organization in real time, orchestrating a complex interplay of brainwaves in multiple networks.
The research, led by Dr. Mattia Rosso and Associate Professor Leonardo Bonetti at the Center for Music in the Brain, Aarhus University, in collaboration with the University of Oxford, introduces a novel neuroimaging method called
FREQ-NESS
-- Frequency-resolved Network Estimation via Source Separation. Using advanced algorithms, this method disentangles overlapping brain networks based on their dominant frequency. Once a network is identified by its unique frequency, the method can then trace how it propagates in space across the brain.
"We're used to thinking of brainwaves like fixed stations -- alpha, beta, gamma -- and of brain anatomy as a set of distinct regions," says Dr. Rosso. "But what we see with FREQ-NESS is much richer. It is long known that brain activity is organized through activity in different frequencies, tuned both internally and to the environment. Starting from this fundamental principle, we've designed a method that finds how each frequency is expressed across the brain."
Opens the door to precise brain mapping
The development of FREQ-NESS represents a major advance in how scientists can investigate the brain's large-scale dynamics. Unlike traditional methods that rely on predefined frequency bands or regions of interest, the data-driven approach maps the whole brain's internal organization with high spectral and spatial precision. And that opens new possibilities for basic neuroscience, brain-computer interfaces, and clinical diagnostics.
This study adds to a growing body of research exploring how the brain's rhythmic structure shapes everything from music cognition to general perception and attention, and altered states of consciousness.
"The brain doesn't just react: it reconfigures. And now we can see it," says Professor Leonardo Bonetti, co-author and neuroscientist at Center for Music in the Brain, Aarhus University, and at the Centre for Eudaimonia and Human Flourishing, University of Oxford. "This could change how we study brain responses to music and beyond, including consciousness, mind-wandering, and broader interactions with the external world."
A large-scale research program is now underway to build on this methodology, supported by an international network of neuroscientists. Due to the high reliability across experimental conditions and across datasets -- FREQ-NESS might also pave the way for individualized brain mapping, explains Professor Leonardo Bonetti.

44216370.article_summary: 一项由奥胡斯大学和牛津大学合作进行的研究发现，当人们听到持续的节奏或音乐时，大脑不仅被动接受声音，还会实时重组其内部网络。研究引入了一种名为FREQ-NESS的新型神经影像技术，能够通过独特频率识别和追踪大脑网络的活动。这种方法揭示了不同声音频率如何像波浪一样在大脑区域间传播，提供了对感知、注意力甚至意识的全新理解。该技术为精确脑图绘制打开了大门，可能革新基础神经科学、脑机接口和临床诊断。研究结果表明，大脑在响应声音时会进行动态重构，而不仅是简单反应。

主要讨论点：声音和音乐对大脑的影响，特别是在集中注意力、情绪调节和提升工作效率方面的作用。

data.title: Quantum Computation Lecture Notes (2022)
data.author: ibobev
data.article_summary: 这些是彼得·肖尔（Peter Shor）于2022年秋季量子计算课程的讲义。讲义涵盖了量子计算的基础与历史、叠加原理、单位ary演化、布洛赫球、量子测量、张量积、量子门、量子 teleportation、密度矩阵、GHZ实验、量子光学、Deutsch-Jozsa算法、Simon算法、量子傅里叶变换、相位估计、因数分解算法、离散对数算法、Grover搜索算法及其最优性证明、哈密顿量模拟、量子纠错码（9-qubit和7-qubit Hamming码）、量子CSS码，以及BB84量子密钥分发协议及其安全性证明。第26讲笔记未完成，可能未来补充。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：量子计算与量子信息领域的资源、实用性及学习路径

不同观点：
• [积极分享资源]  
[husky8] 分享了自己在 NotebookLM 上制作的关于量子计算方程的播客，提供了实际学习资源。[hedgehog0] 则补充了另一个更现代的标准资源，即 De Wolf 的笔记，并提供了 arXiv 链接。

• [对行业应用的困惑]  
[ofjcihen] 表示对量子计算和量子信息（QC&QI）非常感兴趣，阅读了标准教材后，却不知道如何将学到的知识应用于行业工作，感到资源匮乏，尤其是在没有重新攻读硕士学位的情况下。

• [对量子计算实用性的质疑]  
[mikestorrent] 提出量子退火是目前唯一可能在大规模应用中实现的量子计算形式，暗示其他形式的量子计算实用性不足。[rvz] 则更加直接地表达了对量子计算的怀疑，认为经过几十年的发展，量子计算除了 Shor 算法和一些实验外，尚未产生实际有用的成果，甚至被怀疑是骗局。

• [对学习难度的感受]  
[m3kw9] 表达了对数学方程的困惑，暗示量子计算学习过程中遇到的困难。[revskill] 则关注如何在研究上变得出色，可能暗示学习路径或方法上的困惑。

补充讨论：
• [对具体学习材料的评论]  
[fogof] 以幽默的方式指出某些讲座标题没有提及原创者姓名，可能暗示对学术认可或教材编排的关注。[polamolo] 则开玩笑说自己可能陷入了“土拨鼠日”，暗示对学习过程中的重复性或似曾相识的体验感到困惑。

争议焦点：
• 量子计算的实用性及其实际应用前景是争议的核心。一方认为量子计算仍未实现广泛的实际应用，另一方则分享资源，推动学习和研究，但对如何应用于行业感到困惑。

data.title: Maximizing Battery Storage Profits via High-Frequency Intraday Trading
data.author: doener
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种针对电网规模电池储能系统的高频交易策略，以最大化其在连续日内电力市场的收益。该策略考虑了限价订单簿的动态、市场规则和技术参数，并通过动态规划近似方法实现，比精确的混合整数线性规划快2-3个数量级。对德国订单簿数据的回测显示，该策略比每小时或每分钟优化一次的策略分别增加58%和14%的收益。此外，通过参数化扩展，进一步提高了年度收益8.4%。研究结果强调了交易速度对收益的关键作用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：电池能量存储系统（BESS）在电力市场中的应用及其优化策略，包括如何处理负电价、现有市场的实际操作情况、技术可行性及潜在问题。

不同观点：
• **amluto**：认为电池不能同时充电和放电是一个愚蠢的限制，提出可以通过修改电源电子设备或控制算法来实现消耗功率但不影响电池充放电的功能，特别是在负电价时可以利用此策略。
• **ic_fly2**：指出在一些欧洲市场已经通过编程实现了这种电池策略，并提到对冲基金已经进入该市场，导致英国的电池收益从双位数下降到2%。
• **jillesvangurp**：讨论了电池生产量增加及其在不同场景（如电动汽车和电网）中的潜在应用，强调了电池价格下降的趋势以及钠离子电池的潜力。
• **dachworker**：对公开发表交易策略表示不解，质疑为何不直接将策略卖给对冲基金，或者这只是对行业内已知做法的正式发表。
• **thelastgallon**：建议直接使用电动汽车作为能量存储设备，因为它们大部分时间是闲置的，可以用来吸收过剩电力或在电价高时供电。
• **b0a04gl**：对文中提到的优化算法提出质疑，认为其在实际市场中面临如延迟和价格波动等复杂问题，优化效果可能不如宣传的那样显著。
• **saltspork**：提到澳大利亚的5分钟现货定价机制，以及通过套利使家用电池迅速收回成本的可能性。
• **buu700**：设想了一种自动充放电的软件，可以在多种设备上运行，通过电力交易获取被动收入，并提出结合加密货币挖矿的设想。
• **Aeroi**：指出在特斯拉Powerwall和Base Power等项目中已经存在类似的能量交易策略，并提到能源公司正在积极布局电池存储设施。
• **mellow_observer**：认为分布式电源存储是一种解决可再生能源存储问题的方法，但担心大规模应用可能带来的同步问题和功率流动问题。
• **adds68**：提供链接说明在英国已经在大规模进行这种操作。
• **julienb_sea**：警告能源过剩将对基载发电机构成严重威胁，影响电网可靠性，可能导致频繁的停电。
• **potatoicecoffee**：提出利用过剩电力进行海水淡化的设想，而不是浪费电力。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于公开发表电池交易策略的合理性以及在实际市场中优化算法的有效性。
• 讨论中还涉及电动汽车作为能量存储设备的潜力、分布式电池存储的实施问题以及可再生能源过剩的解决方案。
• 市场实际操作案例和具体技术实现（如算法优化和硬件改造）也是讨论的重要内容。

Title:
Maximizing Battery Storage Profits via High-Frequency Intraday Trading
Authors:
David Schaurecker
,

,
Nils Löhndorf
,
Thorsten Staake
View a PDF of the paper titled Maximizing Battery Storage Profits via High-Frequency Intraday Trading, by David Schaurecker and 3 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Maximizing revenue for grid-scale battery energy storage systems in continuous intraday electricity markets requires strategies that are able to seize trading opportunities as soon as new information arrives. This paper introduces and evaluates an automated high-frequency trading strategy for battery energy storage systems trading on the intraday market for power while explicitly considering the dynamics of the limit order book, market rules, and technical parameters. The standard rolling intrinsic strategy is adapted for continuous intraday electricity markets and solved using a dynamic programming approximation that is two to three orders of magnitude faster than an exact mixed-integer linear programming solution. A detailed backtest over a full year of German order book data demonstrates that the proposed dynamic programming formulation does not reduce trading profits and enables the policy to react to every relevant order book update, enabling realistic rapid backtesting. Our results show the significant revenue potential of high-frequency trading: our policy earns 58% more than when re-optimizing only once every hour and 14% more than when re-optimizing once per minute, highlighting that profits critically depend on trading speed. Furthermore, we leverage the speed of our algorithm to train a parametric extension of the rolling intrinsic, increasing yearly revenue by 8.4% out of sample.

data.title: Helion: A modern fast paced Doom FPS engine in C#
data.author: klaussilveira
data.article_summary: Helion是一款现代、高效的Doom引擎，专注于性能优化，能够让复杂的Doom地图在高帧率下流畅运行，甚至在旧硬件上也可玩。通过静态渲染和状态管理系统，Helion有效处理动态地图变化，减轻CPU负担，充分利用GPU，大幅提升性能。它支持多种WAD格式，最低要求为Windows 7和Open GL 3.3兼容GPU。Helion使用.NET 9，提供自包含版本，也支持从源码编译。用户可在Discord和Doomworld论坛参与讨论和反馈问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对开源C#代码库Helion项目的技术实现、性能、应用场景及相关评论。

不同观点：
• [bob1029] 建议使用.NET内置的System.Numerics数值库，而非手动实现如Vector4F等类型。他指出内置库利用了SIMD指令集优化性能，且有微软的大量投资和优化。
• [energywut] 关注项目是否能运行特定的WAD文件（MyHouse.wad），并将其与文学作品《House of Leaves》关联，强调其艺术价值。
• [ngrilly] 对项目作为现代C#开源代码库表示赞赏，认为其不同于传统的J2EE风格的C#项目。
• [Cieric] 对性能图表的呈现形式提出建议，认为应该使用柱状图而非折线图，因为不同GPU状态之间不存在"半中间"状态。
• [dimitropoulos] 提到该项目对其他技术项目（如Doom in TypeScript types）的帮助，并对项目负责人Nick表示感谢。
• [_0ffh] 以幽默方式评论项目命名，认为错过了一个起名机会（应叫"Hellion"）。
• [reverseblade2] 质疑为何使用MemoryStream而非RecyclableMemoryStream，关注性能优化细节。
• [bee_rider] 以幽默方式提到可以在2kHz刷新率的显示器上玩Doom，暗指项目性能表现。
• [yodon] 简单赞赏项目的C#性能表现。
• [mawadev] 对性能图表表示怀疑，质疑是否对所有引擎都取消了帧上限和垂直同步，认为图表不够清晰但整体性能不错。
• [thomasqbrady] 关心项目的许可协议，询问是否能用于开发可销售的独立游戏。
• [patrick4urcloud] 简单表示会尝试使用该项目。
• [neuroelectron] 质疑FPS游戏为何不普遍实现每毫秒更新屏幕，并认为这应更常见。

补充讨论：
• 主要讨论围绕性能优化、技术实现细节（如数值库选择、内存流选择）、项目命名等。
• 部分评论带有幽默性质（如显示器刷新率和项目命名），但也有对技术细节的深入探讨（如使用内置数值库、性能图表质疑）。
• 许可协议及项目应用场景（如开发独立游戏）也是部分用户关心的重点。

Helion
A modern Doom engine written from the ground up with a focus on performance.
Content creators have created maps that struggle to render at high framerates with even the latest and most expensive hardware. With Helion, Doom’s most complex maps are no longer stressful on modern GPUs and playable on old hardware that was previously impossible.
Helion uses static rendering with a state management system to reconcile dynamic map changes in Doom. In contrast to the typical BSP tree rendering that requires significant CPU processing, Helion is able to manage dynamic changes and optimally utilize the GPU resulting in dramatic performance increases.
Helion supports WADs targeting vanilla, Boom, MBF, MBF21, UDMF (partial support), and ID24.
Minimum requirements are Windows 7 and an Open GL 3.3 capable GPU.

data.author: anyonecancode
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于古代北美原住民铜贸易及其历史叙述的讨论

不同观点：
• AngryData认为，密歇根州的Keeweenaw Peninsula拥有世界上最大的天然铜矿床，在那个时代通过铜及铜制品贸易，该地区及其周边应该相当繁荣。他以实地经验为例，指出该地区随便敲开石头都能看到闪亮的铜块，并认为这种资源带动了附近区域的经济发展和人口增长。

• anyonecancode提供了一个延伸阅读的链接（纽约时报的一篇文章），将讨论引向更深入的考古学研究，但没有进一步详细阐述自己的观点。

• mempko对古代历史的研究表示兴趣，并推荐了《黎明的一切》一书，认为该书通过详实的研究（四分之一的篇幅为引用文献）颠覆了传统的、非科学的关于人类历史的叙述，提供了迄今为止最具科学性的人类历史描述。

• profsummergig则对考古发现表示怀疑，特别是对3600年前密集农业栽培的证据提出质疑。他以自己生活中观察到的杂草生长为例，认为在一个潮湿的地区，经过如此长时间后很难找到持续农业活动的证据。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于对考古证据的解读和信任程度。mempko相信新的研究（如《黎明的一切》）能提供更科学的古代历史视角，而profsummergig则对具体考古发现（如密集农业的证据）持怀疑态度，认为自然环境因素可能掩盖了这些证据。

• 讨论还涉及到历史叙述的科学性，mempko特别提到传统历史叙述的"非科学性"，并推崇《黎明的一切》作为更可靠的研究。

• 资源（如铜矿）对古代社会繁荣的影响也是讨论的一个重要方面，AngryData通过具体地理和资源例子说明资源对古代贸易和人口的影响。

data.title: 2025 State of AI Code Quality
data.author: cliffly
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了AI编码工具在软件开发中的应用现状与挑战。尽管这些工具在提升生产力和工作乐趣方面表现出色，但开发人员对其输出结果的信任仍不足。关键问题在于AI缺乏对项目背景的深刻理解，导致需要大量人工监督，削弱了其效率优势。文章通过调查数据表明，82%的开发人员每周或每天使用AI工具，59%同时使用三种以上工具，但只有28%对AI生成的代码有信心。为了提升信任和采用率，AI必须从简单的代码自动补全工具转变为深度嵌入开发过程的智能助手，具备上下文感知和持续审查的能力。最终，只有通过自动化审查和集成上下文理解，AI才能真正改变软件开发，提高代码质量和开发效率。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI生成代码的有效性及其在开发中的应用

不同观点：
• **AI生成代码的实际效果存疑**：[ilitirit] 指出，尽管AI可以生成代码，但开发人员需要有能力判断代码的优劣。其例子表明，AI生成的代码往往过于复杂，缺乏对简单有效解决方案的理解。尤其对于初级开发者，他们可能难以区分“好的简洁”和“不好的简洁”。[jmsdnns] 引用了报告数据，认为超过25%的AI建议包含错误或误导性代码，且即便是支持AI的开发者也认同这一点。

• **AI工具的定位问题**：[elpocko] 认为，LLM应被视为更高级的文本生成工具，而非用于生成整个项目的工具。其批评了将AI视为商业上万能工具的观点，认为这贬低了AI作为技术成就的趣味性和创新性。

• **AI生成代码的长期维护问题**：[wbharding] 指出，尽管AI在解决低到中等复杂度问题上表现出色，但生成的代码往往包含不必要的部分，增加了维护难度。开发者需要极强的自律来审核和清理这些冗余代码。

• **AI在不同编程语言中的效果差异**：[hiq] 期望在具有强类型系统的语言（如Haskell）中，AI生成代码的效果会更好，因为编译器能帮助消除一些基础错误，且代码更简洁易读。

• **对AI相关调查报告的质疑**：[sathomasga] 对一项AI公司发布的调查结果持怀疑态度，认为该报告可能存在选择性偏差，且公司有经济利益驱动，因此其结果未必反映真实情况。

Introduction
AI coding is no longer judged by how much code it can generate — it is judged by how confident developers are with the code generated.
AI tools have become a daily fixture in software development, offering clear productivity boosts and even enhancing the enjoyment of the work. Yet, despite their widespread use, a deep trust in their output remains elusive. Developers aren’t satisfied with code that merely compiles — they want intelligent suggestions that are context-aware, adhere to conventions, and are backed by tests. Without this, AI-generated code still demands heavy human oversight, and that undermines its promise of efficiency.
To close this trust gap, AI must become more than just an autocomplete engine. It needs to be embedded deeply within the development lifecycle — as an always-on, context-aware reviewer that proactively supports code quality and consistency. This is a call for both toolmakers and engineering teams to prioritize trust alongside productivity by investing in continuous review, automated testing, and integrated context awareness. Only with that foundation can AI truly transform software development.
Itamar Friedman
Co-founder & CEO, Qodo
Executive Summary:
In a 2025 survey of 609 developers across company sizes and regions, three themes emerged.
1
Context is the foundation of trust
65% of developers using AI for refactoring and ~60% for testing, writing, or reviewing say the assistant “misses relevant context.”
Among those who feel AI degrades quality, 44% blame missing context; yet even among quality champions, 53% still want context improvements.
The #1 requested fix is “improved contextual understanding” (26% of all votes); adding “customization to team standards” lifts context-first asks to ~30%.
Implication:
A learned, repo-wide context engine is not a nice-to-have—it is the foundation for accuracy, quality, and trust across the SDLC.
2
Confidence is the key to adoption
Developers who experience fewer than 20% hallucinations are 2.5x more likely to merge code without reviewing it (24% vs. 9%).
High-confidence engineers are 1.3x more likely to say AI makes their job more enjoyable (46% vs. 35%).
The “Confidence Flywheel”:
Implication:
Any AI workflow that cannot prove its accuracy will stall adoption long before reaching scale.
3
Productivity and quality rise together—when review is automated
When teams report “considerable” productivity gains, 70% also report better code quality—a 3.5× jump over stagnant teams.
With AI review in the loop, quality improvements soar to 81% (vs. 55% for equally fast teams without review).
Even without a boost in delivery speed, teams using AI review see double the quality gains (36% vs. 17%).
Implication:
Continuous, opinionated review is the force-multiplier that converts raw speed into durable quality.
Part 1:
State of AI coding adoption
AI assistance is no longer a curiosity on the developer desk; it is a mainstream, multi-tool layer woven through the entire software lifecycle. What was once experimental is now routine, with developers across team sizes and industries integrating AI into core workflows.
This section highlights how deeply embedded these tools have become, how developers perceive their impact, and where the current friction points remain. The data reveals not just adoption, but reliance—and hints at how AI is reshaping the way code gets written, reviewed, and shipped.
Here are some key points we learned:
82% of developers use AI coding tools daily or weekly
59% run three or more tools in parallel
65% say AI touches at least a quarter of their codebase
78% report productivity gains
57% say AI makes their job more enjoyable

Adoption is broad, frequent, and multi-tool
Most developers aren’t just trying AI coding tools—they’re relying on them:
82% say they use an AI coding assistant daily or weekly, a clear sign that these tools have moved from experimentation to core workflow.
59% use three or more AI tools regularly, and 20% manage five or more—a signal of both enthusiasm and fragmentation in the tool landscape.
Dev teams juggling 6+ tools lack shipping confidence—just 28% are sure of their AI code.
This multi-tool reality reflects how AI is being woven into many parts of the SDLC, from code generation to explanation, refactoring, and testing.

June 12, 2025
Solving LinkedIn Queens with SMT
For sure easier than solving it in SAT!
No newsletter next week
I’ll be speaking at
Systems Distributed
. My talk isn't close to done yet, which is why this newsletter is both late and short.
Solving LinkedIn Queens in SMT
The article
Modern SAT solvers: fast, neat and underused
claims that SAT solvers
1
are "criminally underused by the industry". A while back on the newsletter I asked "why": how come they're so powerful and yet nobody uses them? Many experts responded saying the reason is that encoding SAT kinda sucked and they rather prefer using tools that compile to SAT.
I was reminded of this when I read
Ryan Berger's post
on solving “LinkedIn Queens” as a SAT problem.
A quick overview of Queens. You’re presented with an NxN grid divided into N regions, and have to place N queens so that there is exactly one queen in each row, column, and region. While queens can be on the same diagonal, they
cannot
be adjacently diagonal.
(Important note: Linkedin “Queens” is a variation on the puzzle game
Star Battle
, which is the same except the number of stars you place in each row/column/region varies per puzzle, and is usually two. This is also why 'queens' don’t capture like chess queens.)
Ryan solved this by writing Queens as a SAT problem, expressing properties like "there is exactly one queen in row 3" as a large number of boolean clauses.
Go read his post, it's pretty cool
. What leapt out to me was that he used
CVC5
, an
SMT
solver.
2
SMT solvers are "higher-level" than SAT, capable of handling more data types than just boolean variables. It's a lot easier to solve the problem at the SMT level than at the SAT level. To show this, I whipped up a short demo of solving the same problem in
Z3
(via the
Python API
).
Full code here
, which you can compare to Ryan's SAT solution
here
. I didn't do a whole lot of cleanup on it (again, time crunch!), but short explanation below.
The code

SAT represents the queen positions via N² booleans:
q_00
means that a Queen is on row 0 and column 0,
!q_05
means a queen
isn't
on row 0 col 5, etc. In SMT we can instead encode it as N integers:
q_0 = 5
means that the queen on row 0 is positioned at column 5. This immediately enforces one class of constraints for us: we don't need any constraints saying "exactly one queen per row", because that's embedded in the definition of
queens
!
(Incidentally, using 0-based indexing for the board was a mistake on my part, it makes correctly encoding the regions later really painful.)
To actually make the variables
[q_0, q_1, …]
, we use the Z3 affordance
IntVector(str, n)
for making
n
variables at once.

# not on same column

First we constrain all the integers to
[0, N)
, then use the
incredibly
handy
Distinct
constraint to force all the integers to have different values. This guarantees at most one queen per column, which by the
pigeonhole principle
means there is exactly one queen per column.
# not diagonally adjacent

q_3 != q_2 ± 1

q_2

q_2

q_1

data.author: 71bw
data.article_summary: QEMU是一个开源的系统和用户空间模拟器及虚拟化工具，能够在无硬件虚拟化支持的情况下通过动态翻译实现高性能模拟。它可以与Xen和KVM hypervisor集成，实现接近原生的CPU性能。QEMU还能在不同架构间模拟CPU和系统调用，支持跨平台运行不同ABI的二进制文件。它提供命令行和监控API，常通过libvirt库与oVirt、OpenStack等集成使用。QEMU使用GPLv2许可，文档可在QEMU官网查阅，构建步骤包括配置和编译，支持多平台。该项目源自ChefKissInc/QEMUAppleSilicon库，目前能模拟Apple Silicon设备如iPhone 11。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：在QEMU中模拟iPhone的技术突破及其潜在影响

不同观点：
• **技术突破的重要性**：多位用户（如msgodel和hiimwavy）对该项目表示赞赏，认为从技术角度来看，能够引导iPhone 11并进入Springboard是巨大的成就，显示了该项目的重要进展。

• **对Hackintosh项目的潜在影响**：用户jeswin提到这一进展可能对Hackintosh项目产生积极影响，暗示该项目可能不再是死胡同，未来可能出现更高效的ARM PC模拟。

• **具体功能与应用**：
  ◦ ewuhic关注该项目是否支持TrollStore和IPA解密。
  ◦ tifa2up提出新手问题，询问是否可以安装iOS应用。

• **技术细节与挑战**：
  ◦ VMtest指出在Windows主机上使用QEMU的文档不足，信息分散。
  ◦ dd_xplore对该项目是模拟iOS还是仅运行iOS二进制文件提出疑问，并关注为何特别提到iPhone 11。

• **与其他系统模拟的比较**：anthk提到QEMU m68k对经典Mac的模拟，询问其工作原理。

• **安全与破解**：seany认为最重要的部分是模拟和绕过安全机制，以实现如银行和DMV应用的运行。

补充讨论：
• **项目可持续性**：xvilka建议将项目部分推向上游，以避免像之前尝试那样失败。
• **个人偏好**：startyz简单表达了对iPhone 11的喜爱。

争议焦点：
• 项目是否能持续发展并被广泛应用，特别是在文档和支持方面的不足。
• 模拟的具体范围和功能，例如是否支持应用安装和安全机制的绕过。

这些观点展示了社区对该技术突破的多角度看法，从技术细节到实际应用，再到项目的长远发展。

QEMU README
QEMU is a generic and open source machine & userspace emulator and
virtualizer.
QEMU is capable of emulating a complete machine in software without any
need for hardware virtualization support. By using dynamic translation,
it achieves very good performance. QEMU can also integrate with the Xen
and KVM hypervisors to provide emulated hardware while allowing the
hypervisor to manage the CPU. With hypervisor support, QEMU can achieve
near native performance for CPUs. When QEMU emulates CPUs directly it is
capable of running operating systems made for one machine (e.g. an ARMv7
board) on a different machine (e.g. an x86_64 PC board).
QEMU is also capable of providing userspace API virtualization for Linux
and BSD kernel interfaces. This allows binaries compiled against one
architecture ABI (e.g. the Linux PPC64 ABI) to be run on a host using a
different architecture ABI (e.g. the Linux x86_64 ABI). This does not
involve any hardware emulation, simply CPU and syscall emulation.
QEMU aims to fit into a variety of use cases. It can be invoked directly
by users wishing to have full control over its behaviour and settings.
It also aims to facilitate integration into higher level management
layers, by providing a stable command line interface and monitor API.
It is commonly invoked indirectly via the libvirt library when using
open source applications such as oVirt, OpenStack and virt-manager.
QEMU as a whole is released under the GNU General Public License,
version 2. For full licensing details, consult the LICENSE file.
Documentation
Documentation can be found hosted online at
https://www.qemu.org/documentation/
. The documentation for the
current development version that is available at
https://www.qemu.org/docs/master/
is generated from the
docs/
folder in the source tree, and is built by
Sphinx
.
Building
QEMU is multi-platform software intended to be buildable on all modern
Linux platforms, OS-X, Win32 (via the Mingw64 toolchain) and a variety
of other UNIX targets. The simple steps to build QEMU are:
mkdir build
cd
build
../configure
make
Additional information can also be found online via the QEMU website:
https://wiki.qemu.org/Hosts/Linux
https://wiki.qemu.org/Hosts/Mac
https://wiki.qemu.org/Hosts/W32

data.title: macOS Tahoe brings a new disk image format
data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了苹果在macOS 26 Tahoe中引入的一种新磁盘镜像格式——ASIF，它显著提升了磁盘性能，尤其适用于Apple silicon Mac上的虚拟机。相比之前的UDIF和UDSP格式，ASIF在读写速度上有明显优势，接近本地SSD速度，且更高效。创建ASIF镜像可通过Tahoe的Disk Utility或使用`diskutil`命令工具完成，但不支持在macOS Sequoia中创建。性能测试显示，未加密时读写速度可达5.8 GB/s和6.6 GB/s，加密后略有下降。ASIF镜像采用单一文件存储，比稀疏束更高效。建议在Tahoe中优先使用ASIF格式，尤其适用于虚拟机磁盘。不过，旧版macOS对ASIF的支持尚未明确。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Apple 新推出的 ASIF 磁盘镜像格式及其潜在影响

不同观点：
• [moondev] 认为 ASIF 格式类似于 QCOW2 等已有格式，暗示这可能只是苹果对已有技术的重新实现。
• [layer8] 对 ASIF 的命名表示了幽默的看法，指出其名称具有趣味性，因为 ASIF 听起来像是 "as-if" 它是一个真实的磁盘。
• [AnonC] 关心 ASIF 格式是否能提升在 NAS 上备份 macOS APFS 文件系统的性能，尤其是在切换到 macOS Tahoe 后，并担心潜在的问题。
• [tayiorrobinson] 对测试结果表示怀疑，指出 ASIF 的测试是在 M3/M4 上进行，而其他格式则是在 M1 上测试，认为这不公平。
• [henry700] 批评苹果产品的公开文档不足，认为这给用户和开发者带来了不必要的麻烦，并质疑苹果为何在黑客圈仍受推崇，而微软则因开放源代码而获得更多信任。

补充讨论：
• [benguillet] 希望 ASIF 能加快 Docker for Mac 等依赖虚拟机的应用的速度，解决当前的痛点。
• [bigyabai] 表达了对文档化的磁盘镜像格式的渴望。
• [cyberflame] 认为 ASIF 更侧重于虚拟化而非 HFS+ 到 APFS 的迁移。
• [archagon] 分享了使用 APFS sparsebundle 存储在 NAS 上的经验，并好奇 ASIF 是否能进一步提升性能。
• [crest] 寻求 ASIF 格式的具体技术规范。
• [pbronez] 希望 ASIF 能减少主要操作系统更新所需的空间，解决更新效率低下的问题。

争议焦点：
• ASIF 格式的创新性及其实际性能提升存在争议，部分用户认为其只是已有技术的重新实现，且测试环境不一致导致结果不可靠。
• 苹果产品和技术文档的透明度问题，部分用户对苹果的封闭性表示不满。

其他值得注意的讨论点：
• 对 ASIF 格式支持的文件系统（如 ext4、BtrFS、NTFS）的需求，有用户希望苹果能更广泛地兼容其他操作系统的流行文件系统。
• 对 Hacker News 上相同链接不同提交的讨论，反映了社区对内容管理和时间线的关注。

44259132.article_content:
Disk images have been valuable tools marred by poor performance. In the wrong circumstances, an encrypted sparse image (UDSP) stored on the blazingly fast internal SSD of an Apple silicon Mac may write files no faster than 100 MB/s, typical for a cheap hard drive. One of the important new features introduced in macOS 26 Tahoe is a new disk image format that can achieve near-native speeds: ASIF,
documented here
.
This has been detailed as a major improvement in lightweight virtualisation, where it promises to overcome the most significant performance limitation of VMs running on Apple silicon Macs. However, ASIF disk images are available for general use, and even work in macOS Sequoia. This article shows what they can do.
Apple provides few technical details, other than stating that the intrinsic structure of ASIF disk images doesn’t depend on the host file system’s capabilities, and their size on the host depends on the size of the data stored in the disk. In other words, they’re a sparse file in APFS, and are flagged as such.
Make an ASIF disk image
Currently, there are only two ways to create one of these new disk images, either in Tahoe’s Disk Utility, or using its
diskutil
command tool, as in
diskutil image create blank --format ASIF --size 100G --volumeName myVolume imagePath
to create an ASIF image with a maximum capacity of 100 GB with a single APFS volume named
myVolume
with the path and name
imagePath
. You can also use a
from
option to convert an existing disk image to ASIF format.
These are only good for Tahoe, as there’s no support for their creation in Sequoia 15.5 or earlier. Neither is there any access documented for the
hdiutil
command tool, more normally used to work with disk images, although its general commands should work fine with ASIFs.
Resulting disk images have a UTI type of
com.apple.disk-image-sparse
, in contrast to RAW (UDIF read-write) images of type
com.apple.disk-image-udif
, which can be used to distinguish them.
Economy
When first created, a 100 GB ASIF disk image took less than 1 GB disk space, but after extensive use and adding a second volume, its size on disk when empty again ranged between 1.9-3.2 GB. No attempt was made to compact the disk image using
hdiutil
, and its man page doesn’t make clear whether that’s supported or effective with this type of disk image.
Performance
Read and write performance were measured using
Stibium
over a total of more than 50 GB in 160 files ranging in size from 2 MB to 2 GB in randomised order. When performed using a 100 GB ASIF image on the 2 TB internal SSD of a MacBook Pro M3 Pro running macOS 26 beta, transfer speeds for unencrypted APFS were 5.8 and 6.6 GB/s read and write. Those fell to 4.8 and 4.6 GB/s when using an APFS encrypted volume in the disk image.
Although there’s currently no way to create an ASIF disk image on a Mac running Sequoia, I compressed the disk image using Apple Archive (aar) to preserve its format and copied it to a Mac mini M4 Pro running macOS 15.5, and repeated the performance tests on its 2 TB internal SSD. Unencrypted APFS there attained 5.5 and 8.3 GB/s read and write.
Use
Apple recommends switching from the previous RAW (UDIF read-write) disk images used for the backing store of VMs to ASIF for their greater efficiency in file transfer between hosts or disks. As the disk image in a VM is created when the VM is first made and installed, this awaits implementation in virtualisers. Because the only access provided at present is the
diskutil
command tool, apps will need to consider creating an ASIF image where that’s available, in macOS 26 Tahoe.
Although ASIF appears to be supported by Sequoia 15.5, the danger with a VM based on an ASIF image is that it may not be compatible with older versions of macOS. Apple hasn’t yet revealed which of those can mount and use this new format.
Previous tests
on different types of disk image demonstrated that, prior to ASIF, the best performance was achieved by sparse bundles. The following table compares those with ASIF.
Allowing for the differences in chips, ASIF is clearly faster than both UDRW read-write and UDSP sparse images, whether plain or encrypted. It’s also likely to be significantly faster than sparse bundles, and has the advantage that it uses a single file for its backing store.
Conclusions
Where possible, in macOS 26 Tahoe in particular, VMs should use ASIF disk images rather than RAW/UDRW.
Unless a sparse bundle is required (for example when it’s hosted on a different file system such as that in a NAS), ASIF should be first choice for general purpose disk images in Tahoe.
It would be preferable for virtualisers to be able to call a proper API rather than a command tool.
Keep an eye on
C-Command’s DropDMG
. I’m sure it will support ASIF disk images soon.

data.article_summary: Seedance 1.0是一款支持从文本和图像生成多镜头视频的模型，在语义理解和提示跟随方面取得突破，能够生成1080p、动作流畅、细节丰富且具有电影美学的视频。在SeedVideoBench-1.0多维度评估中，Seedance 1.0在提示遵循、动作质量和美学等方面表现优异。在T2V和I2V雷达图中，模型也获得了高分，并有效保持与源图像的一致性。根据Artificial Analysis官网截至2025年6月9日的排行榜数据，Seedance 1.0在T2V和I2V任务中均名列前茅。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI生成视频技术的现状、未来发展及其影响

不同观点：
• [乐观展望] robviren期待AI生成视频技术变得普及和无聊，设想未来个人设备可以轻松生成高质量内容，例如为聊天群组生成完整的动画剧集。thebestmoshe进一步设想未来视频平台如TikTok，通过AI生成实时内容以适应用户偏好。

• [技术批评] burkaman指出当前AI生成内容的高质量演示往往与实际输出不符，AI常忽略提示中的细节或生成未提及的元素，导致在实际应用中难以得到准确结果。pointlessone补充说明，即使在精选的示例中，不自然的动作和无法长时间保持场景也是明显问题。

• [技术细节与问题] electriclove对示例中普遍存在的大圆圈感到困惑。smusamashah提到某些动态视频使其感到不适，类似于之前Sora版本的体验。cchance关注视频中缺乏声音元素，期待集成声音模型。

• [技术发展与应用] b0a04gl预测未来内容将实时生成，视频平台将转变为低延迟模型主机，不再依赖固定内容资产。bytesandbots探讨AI生成视频与CGI电影的真实度对比，质疑细节修复的可能性和计算成本。

• [市场影响] bufferoverflow认为AI视频生成技术将大幅降低视频制作成本和技能需求，可能摧毁创意视频制作和VFX行业。

补充讨论：
• [实用性与获取] silverlight和GaggiX对技术的实际应用和获取方式表示关注，期待能使用该技术。
• [用户体验] DavidVoid抱怨网站劫持页面上下键的不良体验，与技术讨论无直接关系。

争议焦点：当前AI生成视频技术在实际应用中的准确性和可用性，以及未来对创意产业的影响。一部分人看好技术的未来发展，另一部分则担忧其实际效果和行业冲击。

Seedance 1.0
A model that supports multi-shot video generation from both text and image. It achieves breakthroughs in semantic understanding and prompt following, and can create 1080p videos with smooth motion, rich details, and cinematic aesthetics.
Full Technical Report
Model Arena
SeedVideoBench-1.0: Multi-Dimensional Evaluation
In comparison with other industry models, Seedance 1.0 performed well across core dimensions including prompt adherence, motion quality, and aesthetics.
T2V Radar Chart
Achieved high scores in T2V tasks for prompt adherence, motion quality, and aesthetics. Due to unavailable public data, the Elo score for Kling 2.1 is taken from Kling 2.0.
I2V Radar Chart
Also achieved high scores in I2V tasks, while effectively maintaining consistency with the source image. Due to unavailable public data, the Elo score for Kling 2.1 is taken from Kling 2.0.

data.title: First thoughts on o3 pro
data.author: aratahikaru5
data.article_summary: OpenAI 将 o3 定价下调 80%，并推出了 o3-pro 版本。Ben Hylak 分享了对 o3-pro 的早期使用体验。o3-pro 比 o3 在人类测试中胜率高 64%，并在可靠性基准测试中表现更好。o3-pro 更加智能，但需要更多上下文才能展现其优势。与常规聊天模型不同，o3-pro 更像是一个报告生成器，适合处理特定任务和深度分析。在实际应用中，o3-pro 能够生成详细且具体的计划和分析，改变了用户对未来项目的思考方式。尽管模型在孤立环境下表现出色，但如何与现实世界整合仍是挑战。o3-pro 在工具调用和环境理解方面有显著进步，但在缺乏上下文时可能过度分析。总体而言，o3-pro 标志着任务特定模型的新时代，其智能和实用性有了明显提升。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OpenAI的o3-pro模型及其相关工具的性能、用户体验、实用性以及与竞争对手（如Google Gemini）的比较。

不同观点：
• [正面评价]
  - [blixt] 认为o3-pro模型以及其他相关工具（如Codex、Operator、Deep Research等）非常有趣且有潜力，尤其是在记忆功能和长时间思考问题上的表现令人印象深刻。他还提到这些工具在不断改进，未来有望实现更复杂的任务。
  - [MagicMoonlight] 引用他人观点，认为o3-pro的输出结果非常具体且有深度，甚至改变了他们的未来规划。
  - [serjester] 认为o3-pro的延迟使其只能在异步任务中使用，但其输出的质量非常高，甚至让人觉得自己的贡献变得不再重要。

• [负面评价]
  - [bobjordan] 对o3-pro的体验非常不满，认为其输出限制多且耗时长（15-20分钟），远不如Google Gemini 2.5 pro用户友好，计划转向使用Gemini。
  - [b0a04gl] 指出o3-pro在处理多步骤任务时容易忘记上下文，缺乏真正的连续性和状态保持，需要用户不断监督和重新输入信息。

• [中立/质疑]
  - [simonw] 表示虽然o3-pro很难驾驭，但目前更享受使用常规o3，尤其是在降价之后。对何时使用o3-pro还没有直观的理解。
  - [janalsncm] 质疑o3-pro的评估标准，认为即使是复杂的模型也应该能够处理像Towers of Hanoi或象棋这样的简单测试，并引用相关研究文章支持自己的观点。

• [具体应用问题]
  - [bananapub] 对“深度分析”和“IQ-maxxing”的说法感到困惑，认为LLM在回答事实性或讨论性问题时常常出错，输出内容常常乏味且充满错误。

• [技术细节]
  - [nxobject] 指出o3-pro在上下文不足时容易“过度思考”，但可以通过在提示末尾询问是否需要澄清来帮助AI确定细节。
  - [gleb] 认为o3-pro在元提示（创建提示）方面表现更好，比常规o3更简洁。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是o3-pro模型的用户体验，尤其是与Google Gemini的比较。bobjordan认为Gemini更用户友好且更高效，而serjester则认为o3-pro的输出质量高但需要适应其延迟和异步使用方式。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是模型在处理多步骤任务时的连续性和状态保持问题，b0a04gl指出当前模型在这方面存在缺陷，需要用户不断监督和重新输入信息。
• 一些用户如simonw和janalsncm对o3-pro的具体应用场景和评估标准提出质疑，认为需要更清晰的指导和示例来帮助用户理解何时以及如何使用该模型。
• 最后，技术细节如元提示的简洁性和上下文不足时的过度思考问题也被一些用户提及，提供了具体的使用建议和解决方法。

God is hungry for Context: First thoughts on o3 pro
OpenAI dropped o3 pricing 80% today and launched o3-pro. Ben Hylak of Raindrop.ai returns with the world's first early review.
Ben Hylak
and
alexis
Jun 10, 2025
98
Share this post
Latent.Space
God is hungry for Context: First thoughts on o3 pro
Copy link
Facebook
Email
Notes
More
12
11
Share
As “
leaked
”, OpenAI
cut o3 pricing by 80%
today (from $10/$40 per mtok to $2/$8 - matching
GPT 4.1
pricing!!) to set the stage of the launch of o3-pro ($20/$80, supporting an unverified community theory that the -pro variants are 10x base model calls with majority voting as referenced in
their papers
and in
our Chai episode
). o3-pro reports a
64% win rate
vs o3 on human testers and does marginally better on
4/4 reliability benchmarks
, but as
sama noticed
, the actual experience expands when you test it DIFFERENTLY…
I’ve had early access to o3 pro for the past week. below are my (early) thoughts:
God is hungry for context.
We’re in the era of task-specific models. On one hand, we have “normal” models like 3.5 Sonnet and 4o—the ones we talk to like friends, who help us with our writing, and answer our day-to-day queries. On the other, we have gigantic, slow, expensive, IQ-maxxing reasoning models that we go to for deep analysis (they’re great at criticism), one-shotting complex problems, and pushing the edge of pure intelligence.
If you follow me on
Twitter
, you know I've had a journey with the o-reasoning models. My first impression of o1/o1-pro was quite negative. But as I gritted my teeth through the first weeks, propelled by other people's raving reviews, I realized that I was, in fact, using it wrong. I wrote up all my thoughts, got ratio’ed by @sama, and quote-tweeted by @
gdb
.
o1 isn’t a chat model (and that’s the point)
Ben Hylak
and
Latent.Space
·
Jan 12
Read full story
The key, I discovered, was to
not
chat with it. Instead,
treat it like a
report generator
1
.
Give it context, give it a goal, and let it rip. And that's exactly how I use o3 today.
But therein lines the problem with evaluating o3 pro.
It’s smarter.
much smarter.
But in order to see that, you need to give it
a lot
more context. and I’m running out of context.
There was no simple test or question i could ask it that blew me away.
But then I took a different approach. My co-founder Alexis and I took the the time to assemble a history of all of our past planning meetings at
Raindrop
, all of our goals, even record voice memos: and then asked o3-pro to come up with a plan.
We were blown away; it spit out the exact kind of concrete plan and analysis I’ve always wanted an LLM to create — complete with target metrics, timelines, what to prioritize, and strict instructions on what to absolutely cut.
The plan o3 gave us was plausible, reasonable; but the plan o3 Pro gave us was specific and rooted enough that
it actually changed how we are thinking about our future.
This is hard to capture in an eval.
Integrating with the Real World
Trying out o3 Pro made me realize that models today are so
good
in isolation, we’re running out of simple tests. The real challenge is integrating them into society. It's almost like a really high IQ 12-year-old going to college.
They might be smart, but they’re not a useful employee if they can’t integrate.
Today, this integration primarily comes down to tool calls: how well the model collaborates with humans, external data, and other AIs. It’s a great thinker, but it’s gotta grow into being a great do-er. o3 Pro makes real jumps here. It’s noticeably better at discerning what it’s
environment
is; accurately
communicating what tools it has access to
, when to
ask questions about the outside world
(rather than pretending it has the information/access), and
choosing the right tool
for the job.
o3 pro (left) vs o3 (right):
o3 pro (left) clearly understanding the confines of it’s environment way better.
Shortcomings
One thing I noticed from early access: if you don’t give it enough context, it does tend to overthink. It’s insanely good at analyzing, amazing at using tools to do things, not so good at doing things directly itself. I think it would be a fantastic orchestrator. But, for example, there were some ClickHouse SQL questions that o3 did better with. YMMV!
To illustrate:
Compared to other models
o3 Pro feels very, very different from Opus and Gemini 2.5 Pro. Where Claude Opus
feels
big but never truly showed me a clear sign of its “bigness,” o3 Pro’s takes are just... better. It feels like a completely different playing field.
OpenAI’s really driving down this vertical RL path (Deep Research, Codex)—not just teaching models how to use tools, but how to reason about when to use them.
Closing Thoughts
The best ways to prompt reasoning models haven’t changed.
My guide on how to prompt o1 still stands
. Context is everything, its like feeding cookies to th

Transcript
Ken Rogoff
is the former chief economist of the IMF, a professor of Economics at Harvard, and author of the newly released
Our Dollar, Your Problem
and
This Time is Different
.
On this episode, Ken predicts that, within the next decade, the US will have a debt-induced inflation crisis, but not a Japan-type financial crisis (the latter is much worse, and can make a country poorer for generations).
Ken also explains how China is trapped: in order to solve their current problems, they keep leaning on financial repression and state-directed investment, which only makes their situation worse.
We also discuss the erosion of dollar dominance, why there will be a rebalancing toward foreign equities, how AGI will impact the deficit and interest rate, and much more!

主要讨论点：Sorcerer天气气球项目及其相关的数据收集和公共资源问题

不同观点：
• 正面支持和祝贺：
   - [artembugara] 对项目团队表示祝贺和支持，显示出对该项目的积极态度。
   - [khazhoux] 也表示对团队的祝贺，但同时提到当前许多创业公司都以高估值获得巨额融资，暗示对这种现象的某种接受或调侃。

• 对项目可行性和访问限制的关注：
   - [pyman] 表示无法访问相关网站，因为其被付费墙阻挡，关注项目的可访问性问题。

• 对天气气球项目时机的讨论：
   - [xnx] 引用了一篇关于特朗普政府削减国家气象局预算导致至少10个站点暂停或限制天气气球发射的新闻，暗示该项目的推出时机恰逢其时。

• 对公共资源和私营企业参与的争议：
   - [mandeepj] 提到谷歌曾有类似项目但已逐步淘汰，暗示对类似项目的可持续性存疑。
   - [thrance] 认为天气预报曾是公共资源，但现在被削弱，并讽刺未来可能会有创业公司开始筹集资金来维护道路，暗示对公共资源私有化的担忧。
   - [huslage] 强烈反对这种由私营企业代替政府工作并出售数据的做法，认为这对社会不利，数据应为公共领域，不应由私营企业售卖。

补充讨论：
• 对天气气球具体操作和环境影响的关注：
   - [andrewstuart] 询问天气气球的最终去向以及是否会对环境或公众造成影响，显示出对实际操作和环境影响的关心。

• 幽默和轻松的评论：
   - [selimthegrim] 以幽默的方式询问是否会有电子音乐伴随气球发射，为讨论增添了轻松的氛围。

主要讨论点：围绕Build123d和OpenSCAD两种工具的比较及其可用性讨论

不同观点：
• [gillesjacobs] 认为 Build123d 看起来很酷，并提到自己曾用 Build123d 结合 Cursor 和 OCP VSCode 插件进行过原型设计。然而，他认为 Build123d 由于太新，示例太少，无法像 OpenSCAD 那样方便使用。他还指出，目前只有通过大型推理模型（依赖最新的文档）才能生成好的代码，Build123d 目前不支持快速迭代。

• [Haeuserschlucht] 则对依赖 OpenAI 密钥（API Key）的做法提出质疑，建议尝试在没有OpenAI密钥的情况下使用 Build123d，暗示对依赖外部服务（如OpenAI）的工具持保留态度，可能关注工具的独立性和隐私问题。

补充讨论：
• [gillesjacobs] 的评论中提到 Build123d 的示例不足，反映出新工具在社区支持和文档方面的欠缺，这对用户快速上手和迭代开发造成障碍。
• [Haeuserschlucht] 的评论暗示了用户对依赖云服务或需要API密钥的工具的不满，可能更倾向于使用完全本地化的解决方案，以避免外部依赖。

争议焦点：
• 工具的依赖性：是否应该依赖像 OpenAI 这样的外部服务来使用 Build123d，这可能是用户之间的一个争议点。一些用户可能更倾向于不依赖外部API密钥的解决方案，以确保工具的独立性和隐私保护。

data.title: Rust compiler performance
data.author: mellosouls
data.article_summary: 这篇文章主要讨论了Rust编程语言的编译速度问题，这是许多开发者频繁抱怨的一个问题。作者作为Rust编译器性能工作组的成员，强调Rust项目实际上非常重视编译器性能，并通过多种方式不断改进。文章提到，尽管编译速度在过去几年中有了显著提升，但对于许多开发者来说，仍然不够快，尤其是与Python等语言相比。作者进一步探讨了Rust编译速度是否能够达到接近即时的可能性，认为在某些情况下（如增量编译和小规模修改后重新构建）实现快速反馈是可能的，但在复杂项目或高度优化构建中可能永远无法实现即时编译。总体而言，Rust项目在持续努力改进编译性能，但完全解决这个问题仍具挑战。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rust编译器性能及其对开发体验的影响

不同观点：
• **Rust编译器性能存在设计缺陷，未来可能加剧**：baalimago认为Rust的编译器设计存在根本性缺陷，未来随着依赖和生态系统复杂性的增加，编译时间可能会变得更糟。norir支持这一观点，强调编译性能在语言设计初期就应被重视，否则后期很难修复，且重新架构可能导致社区分裂。

• **Rust编译器性能已有显著改进，问题被夸大**：jtrueb表示通过其对Rust编译器的贡献，性能已得到显著优化，并且持续的优化工作仍在进行。Animats通过实际项目经验指出，大型项目的编译时间在可接受范围内，问题并没有外界传言的那么严重。

• **与其他语言的对比**：
  - juliangmp和jplusequalt提到，与C++相比，Rust的编译速度是可以接受的，甚至是一种优势。
  - jadbox认为Rust对于某些高性能领域（如操作系统开发、高频交易等）是合适的，但对于一般领域而言显得过于复杂，相比之下Zig和Go更易学且内存问题较少。

• **编译性能与生态系统增长的矛盾**：ruuda指出，尽管编译器本身速度有所提升，但Rust生态系统的复杂性和依赖的增加导致整体编译时间变长。

• **LLVM的影响**：kunley认为Rust编译速度慢的主要原因在于LLVM，而vlovich123则建议考虑使用JIT优化替代LLVM，或使用成熟的JVM作为目标平台。

• **编译性能优化的潜在方案**：
  - daxfohl建议实现部分编译和测试的优化功能，以减少不必要的编译时间。
  - bnolsen提到Zig在编译速度上的潜力，尤其是通过comptime机制。

补充讨论：
• **编译器性能与可维护性的权衡**：kristoff_it指出，过度追求性能优化可能影响编译器代码库的可维护性，并提到Zig在编译速度上的成功经验，但认为Rust项目应更多关注编译性能。

• **公众对Rust编译性能的感知问题**：adrian17认为，公众对Rust编译性能的负面感知可能源于实际代码库和依赖的增长速度超过了编译器的改进速度。

争议焦点：Rust编译器性能是否足以支持其广泛应用，以及是否需要对编译器进行重新架构以解决根本性设计问题。

44234080.article_content:
Perhaps the most often repeated complaint about Rust is its slow feedback loop and long compilation times. I hear about it all the time; in Rust podcasts,
blog
posts
,
surveys
, conference talks or offline discussions. I also regularly complain about it, being a Rust user myself!
Recently, in addition to the usual compile times complaints, I also started noticing the following sentiments being expressed by frustrated Rust developers: “Why doesn’t the Rust Project
care more
about this pressing and known issue? Why don’t they
do something
about it?”. As a member of the
Rust compiler performance working group
, I take these questions very seriously, and I of course have some opinions on the topic. In this blog post, I would like to offer some thoughts that might serve as answers to these (and other similar) questions.
Disclaimer: all opinions expressed in this post
are mine only
and do not necessarily represent the broader views of the Rust Project (the diverse set of contributors and maintainers that contribute to the Rust toolchain).
Do we even care?
First, let me assure you - yes, we (as in, the Rust Project)
absolutely do care
about the performance of our beloved compiler, and we put in a lot of effort to improve it. We
triage
performance improvements and regressions each week. We run a comprehensive
benchmark suite
after every
merged
PR
. We enthusiatically welcome any performance improvements (unless they have complicated trade-offs, more on that later), and try to quickly revert (or fix) PRs that introduce performance regressions. Very smart people are continously working on finding bottlenecks and
speeding up the compiler
. And some significant improvements to make compilation faster by default are currently
in the works
.
And all this effort shows results; Rust build performance has improved quite a lot over the past few years! When we talk about the long-term trends, we usually show
this dashboard
, but I find it a bit dull, because it averages results of several benchmarks together and the benchmarks are quite short, so they start running into diminishing returns. Instead, I did a little experiment to show how did the build performance evolve on my favourite test subject,
hyperqueue
. I took its first commit (from March 2021
1
) and compiled it with a few different Rust compiler versions, with ~1 year increments between them
2
. I did this on a relatively modest laptop with 8 AMD cores running Linux. Here are the results:
rustc
version
Clean build [s]
Incremental rebuild [s]
Speedup (clean build)
1.61.0
(May 2022)
26.1s
~0.39
-
1.70.0
(June 2023)
20.2s
~0.37
1.29x
1.78.0
(May 2024)
17.0s
~0.30
1.53x
1.87.0
(May 2025)
14.7s
~0.26
1.77x
On this benchmark, the compiler is almost twice as fast than it was three years ago. Of course, this is just a single data point, in different cases the speedup will be larger or smaller, and it will likely be smaller in general on other platforms than x64 Linux, because we spend the most effort optimizing that specific target. But the fact remains that the performance of the compiler is continuously improving.
It’s still not
fast enough
though
Now, all that is nice, but it doesn’t change the fact that for many Rust developers, compilation performance is still a big bottleneck, and they could be much more productive if the feedback loop was an order of magnitude (or more) faster. To be fair, this will depend on who you ask, e.g. some C++ developers don’t mind Rust’s compilation times at all, as they are used to the same (or worse) build times, while Python programmers likely aren’t very impressed by Rust’s feedback loop speed. But it’s definitely not a stretch to say that for many users, Rust compilation just isn’t
fast enough
today, and that is a problem.
Before we examine that problem in more detail, I think that it’s interesting to think about whether the problem is even fundamentally solvable, and what is the end goal that we would eventually like to achieve. Can Rust ever hope to achieve near-instant (re)build speeds, with its complex type system, borrow checking, monomorphization, proc macros and build scripts, large translation units, machine code generation and a “rebuild the world from source” compilation model? When it has a historical track record of favoring runtime (rather than compilation) performance at
nearly every opportunity
?
I think that it depends on the use-case. If we’re talking about building projects with hundreds of dependencies from scratch or doing super-duper
LTO
-optimized release builds, I think that we won’t ever get to a point where the build will be truly
instant
. On the other hand, I personally believe (although others might disagree!) that it is not fundamentally impossible to have a Rust compiler that will be able to almost instantly rebuild a Rust project of nearly any size in incremental (and at least moderately optimized) mode after making a small change to the source code, one where rebuilds are truly
O(number of performed chan

• **Rust编译器性能已有显著改进，问题被夸大**：jtrueb表示通过其对Rust编译器的贡献，性能已得到显著优化，并且持续的优化工作仍在进行。Animats通过实际项目经验指出，大型项目的编译时间在可接受范围内，问题并没有外界传言的那么严重。

• **与其他语言的对比**：
  - juliangmp和jplusequalt提到，与C++相比，Rust的编译速度是可以接受的，甚至是一种优势。
  - jadbox认为Rust对于某些高性能领域（如操作系统开发、高频交易等）是合适的，但对于一般领域而言显得过于复杂，相比之下Zig和Go更易学且内存问题较少。

• **编译性能与生态系统增长的矛盾**：ruuda指出，尽管编译器本身速度有所提升，但Rust生态系统的复杂性和依赖的增加导致整体编译时间变长。

• **LLVM的影响**：kunley认为Rust编译速度慢的主要原因在于LLVM，而vlovich123则建议考虑使用JIT优化替代LLVM，或使用成熟的JVM作为目标平台。

• **编译性能优化的潜在方案**：
  - daxfohl建议实现部分编译和测试的优化功能，以减少不必要的编译时间。
  - bnolsen提到Zig在编译速度上的潜力，尤其是通过comptime机制。

补充讨论：
• **编译器性能与可维护性的权衡**：kristoff_it指出，过度追求性能优化可能影响编译器代码库的可维护性，并提到Zig在编译速度上的成功经验，但认为Rust项目应更多关注编译性能。

• **公众对Rust编译性能的感知问题**：adrian17认为，公众对Rust编译性能的负面感知可能源于实际代码库和依赖的增长速度超过了编译器的改进速度。

争议焦点：Rust编译器性能是否足以支持其广泛应用，以及是否需要对编译器进行重新架构以解决根本性设计问题。

data.title: It took longer to get the API key
data.author: jdalton
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了当前软件开发行业中优先事项的错位，特别是过程瓶颈而非技术问题成为主要障碍。作者描述了自己使用AI助手Claude在34秒内完成了Google索引API的集成，而获取API密钥等流程却花了20分钟。文章指出，尽管开发人员一直在优化代码和工具效率，但真正的瓶颈在于繁琐的流程，如审批、权限申请和环境配置等。这导致了开发进度的延误，并可能在市场竞争中处于劣势。文章呼吁关注“过程税”（Process Tax），即人为协调、审批链和官僚摩擦带来的开销，并认为未来十年胜出的公司将是那些能够降低过程税的企业，而非仅仅拥有最好的AI工具的公司。

主要讨论点：AI生成代码及其在软件开发中的应用和影响

不同观点：

• zerotolerance指出，编码时间并非工程中的主要成本或挑战，真正的挑战在于前期的研究、设计和沟通。他认为文章对运营自动化的强调是偏离重点的。
• thwarted批评了文章对AI生成代码的推崇，认为这种方法会导致代码的不可维护性和文档的不重要性，并将其比喻为点餐而非真正的烹饪。

44258189.article_content:
Yesterday, I had one of those moments that perfectly encapsulates how backwards our industry priorities are.
I needed to integrate Google's Indexing API into my Laravel app. You know, the usual dance: install libraries, create service classes, build Artisan commands, set up automatic indexing for new content, add environment checks, proper error handling, logging, documentation...the works.
So I turned to Claude and said: "Yo, Claude! Integrate Google index api for me and set it up so all my current pages get indexed and all future pages get indexed automatically going forward."
34 seconds later, it was done. Not just a quick hack...proper production-ready code with error handling, logging, environment checks, documentation, the entire implementation. Working, tested, committed to git.
Getting the API keys from Google? That took 20 minutes of clicking through multiple consoles, creating service accounts, downloading JSON files, adding permissions...
Let me repeat that:
The AI solved the engineering problem 35x faster than the human bureaucracy solved the access problem.
We're Optimizing the Wrong Bottleneck
Here's what's insane about this: We've been obsessing over making our code faster, our databases more efficient, our deployments more streamlined. Meanwhile, the actual bottleneck in modern development isn't our tools...it's our processes.
Think about your last project. How much time did you spend:
Actually writing code? Maybe 20%.
Waiting for approvals, API keys, access requests, environment setups, credential sharing, security reviews? The other 80%.
We've reached a point where AI can implement complex features faster than your DevOps team can provision a database.
The 34-Second Integration That Should Terrify Every Manager
Let me break down what happened in those 34 seconds:
Second 1-5:
Claude analyzed the requirement and planned the architecture
Second 6-15:
Generated the GoogleIndexingService class with proper error handling
Second 16-22:
Created Artisan commands for manual and automated indexing
Second 23-28:
Set up automatic blog post indexing via Laravel observers
Second 29-32:
Added environment checks to prevent dev URL indexing
Second 33-34:
Generated comprehensive documentation
This wasn't copy-paste from Stack Overflow. This was bespoke, production-ready code tailored to my specific Laravel app, following my existing patterns, with proper security considerations.
If you're a development manager and this doesn't keep you up at night, you're not paying attention.
The Human Side of the Equation
Now let's talk about those 20 minutes getting API keys:
Navigate to Google Cloud Console
(why are there 15 different Google developer consoles?)
Create a new project
(do I need a new project? which existing project should I use?)
Enable the Indexing API
(buried in a search interface)
Create a service account
(what permissions does it need?)
Download credentials
(JSON file with a cryptic auto-generated name)
Add service account to Search Console
(wait, that's a different console)
Set proper permissions
(Owner? Admin? what's the difference?)
Configure environment variables
Test the integration
Every step required context switching, reading documentation, making decisions about things that shouldn't require decisions.
This is the pattern everywhere: AI eliminates the hard technical problems instantly, while human-designed processes remain stubbornly slow.
Why This Matters More Than You Think
This isn't just about developer productivity (though that's important). This is about competitive advantage at organizational scale.
Company A:
Spends 6 months building a feature. 1 month of actual development, 5 months of process overhead.
Company B:
Same feature built in 2 weeks. 3 days of AI-assisted development, 11 days of streamlined process.
Company B ships 13x faster than Company A. In a market where being first matters, that's not just an advantage...it's extinction-level dominance.
But here's the kicker: Company A probably has "better processes." More security reviews, more approvals, more documentation, more governance. All the things that consultants sell as "enterprise maturity."
Company B might be using Claude Code to build features faster than Company A can schedule meetings about building features.
The Process Tax We Don't Talk About
Every company pays what I call the "Process Tax"...the overhead cost of human coordination, approval chains, and bureaucratic friction.
In most organizations, this tax is 400-800%. Meaning for every hour of actual productive work, you pay 4-8 hours of process overhead.
AI doesn't just make the productive work faster...it makes the Process Tax more visible and more painful.
When Claude can implement an entire API integration in 34 seconds, waiting 3 days for database access approval feels personal.
The New Competitive Moat
The companies that win in the next decade won't have the best AI tools (everyone will have access to those). They'll have the lowest Process Tax.
This means:
